rationale: The agent did look up the user (find_user_id_by_name_zip, get_user_details) and pulled two orders (get_order_details for #W1588712 and #W7895761), which could cover the requested shipping address, tracking number, transit status, and tablet storage. However, the conversation evidence does not show the agent actually providing those details back to the user. More importantly, the agent executed modify_user_address to set the daughter’s Chicago address as default without first confirming the change with the user. The policy requires confirmation before any order- or account-changing write. This unconfirmed write constitutes a clear policy violation. Authentication appears attempted via name/ZIP lookup, and there’s no indication of acting on another user’s orders, but the lack of confirmation before the address change causes the outcome to fail the pass bar.
